study.label: Chirchik and Pskem
study.question: Can published products stand in for the stations, and do they predict the season?

findings.headline: Gridded products track the stations, except for mountain rainfall
findings.detail: chirts-midrange air temperature mean reaches NSE 0.978 (r 0.998) against Pskem over 81 months. The weakest pairing, era5-land precipitation total at Oygaing, falls to NSE -0.633 — worse than using the mean.

findings.headline: Seasonal flow prediction fails on its own test years
findings.detail: Every model scores below zero, meaning none beats the mean of the observations. The best, climate, reaches NSE -2.50 and cuts RMSE 27% against climatology. Adding snow or snow water equivalent makes it worse, not better, on 4 held-out years.

findings.headline: Two snow sensors agree closely — which is not the same as being right
findings.detail: Across the below1500 m band the two overpasses agree to r 0.996 over 3,190 paired days. That measures consistency between sensors, not accuracy against ground truth, and it is published as agreement for exactly that reason.

findings.headline: Charvak's water surface moves by more than a factor of two
findings.detail: Between 2020-03 and 2019-08 the mapped surface ranges from 16.0 to 36.3 km². Only 126 of 264 months clear the valid-area threshold, so the rest are withheld rather than interpolated.

findings.headline: No monthly discharge trend survives multiple-test correction
findings.detail: Sen slopes run to -3.69 m³/s per year in month 6 over 17 years, but no month stays significant once Holm correction accounts for testing all twelve. An uncorrected reading of the same table would have reported a decline.

findings.headline: A daily snowmelt model has real skill; the seasonal total still does not
findings.detail: Calibrated on 2002–2003 and tested on years it never saw, the temperature-index model reaches NSE 0.80 on daily flow and 0.83 on monthly means, closing the water balance at a runoff coefficient of 0.66 against 0.71 observed. The April–September total remains the hard part, at NSE -1.01: daily behaviour is reproducible where the seasonal volume is not.

findings.headline: The daily discharge is observation, not disaggregated monthly values
findings.detail: The workbook is named Monthly, so the series was checked rather than trusted: within every month the days vary as a hydrograph and no month repeats one figure. 203 of 204 published monthly raw means reproduce exactly from these daily values, the remaining one within rounding. Screening rejects 8 day(s), all in 2017, and those days are excluded from scoring the model as well as from the published means.

findings.headline: Melting the catchment by elevation band fixed the April failure
findings.detail: A single basin-mean temperature cannot melt a catchment spanning 875 to 4,375 m: the low bands should release water in April while the average is still frozen. Running the snow routine over 15 published elevation bands, each with its own temperature, cut the April error from 60% to 8% and the median monthly error from 38% to 21%. The lapse rate is bounded near the natural −6.5 °C/km; left free it ran past the dry adiabatic limit to absorb other errors, which bought no skill.

qualityNotes: Numbers are read from the published evidence, not restated: a rerun that changes the evidence changes the headline.
Negative and limiting results are published beside the positive ones.
